parsed_response.reasoning: Verifiable from the diff: Calendar.d.ts changes the interface to createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number), and only GoogleCalendarService was updated to accept it. LarkCalendarService still declares async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent) and Office365CalendarService async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent). EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now loops destinations and calls createEvent(c, event) / createEvent(c, event, destination.externalId) for each matched credential, but Lark/O365 ignore credentialId and select only the first destinationCalendar (mainHostDestinationCalendar), so the multi-destination routing fix only works for Google. TypeScript method bivariance lets it compile, so this is a half-applied contract/incomplete migration rather than a guaranteed runtime crash — a maintainer should know the array-based multi-calendar support is incomplete for non-Google providers.

judged_text: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId) but only GoogleCalendarService was updated; Lark and Office365 createEvent implementations still declare only (event). TypeScript method bivariance lets this compile, but the contract change is half-applied: a strict-mode or contravariant tightening, or any new service author copying the interface, will pass credentialId that Lark/O365 silently ignore — the multiple-destination fix only works for Google.
